sentences.text: Devan Ramachandran, J.

2. Sri.P.M.Shameer - learned Government Pleader, informs us that the Police have information that the fourth respondent is involved in a Crime, registered as Crime No.185/2020 and numbered as S.C.No.222/2020 before the Additional District Court, Kalpetta, under the provisions of Sections 376 of the IPC read with Section 5 of the POCSO Act and Section 75 of the Juvenile Justice Act; as also in Crime No.97 of 2024 registered under the provisions of Sections 341, 325, 395 of the IPC.

He,
however, conceded that the first case ended in acquittal; but that the State is filing an appeal against the same, for which processes have already been initiated.

He concluded saying that, as regards the second Crime, the fourth respondent has been charge sheeted and is now facing trial on the allegation that he, along with three others, had hijacked a vehicle containing three members of a family and attacked and robbed them of their gold ornaments.

3. The afore information is certainly very distressing; and this is coupled with the submission made before us by the petitioner - who also appeared in person, that he and his wife had been told by the alleged detenue herself that the fourth respondent is a man who indulges in substance abuse and that she had seen it.
He then added that his daughter has been tutored by the fourth respondent; or is under his spell; or acting under threat.

4. However, when we interacted with the alleged 2024:KER:73714 WP(Crl)1037/24 detenue, she denied every one of the afore, saying that the fourth respondent has been "trapped" in all the cases and she then told us with a certain amount of disdain, but bordering on pride, that he has been acquitted in the first case because the victim had turned hostile.

sentences.text: 5. The afore presents before us reasons to exercise caution because, the alleged detenue is merely 19 years in age and is stated to have been with the fourth respondent for the last more than 13 days.

When she says that she wants to go with the fourth respondent, obviously we cannot stop her; but are sure that before we dispose of this matter, a full disclosure of his credentials is required to be given to us by him, as also by the Police.

6. The learned counsel for the fourth respondent submitted that he will file an affidavit answering every allegation impelled against him; and the learned Government Pleader sought ten days time to file an additional report disclosing the credentials of the said respondent.
We grant this.

7. The report furnished by the learned Government Pleader will also contain copies of the judgment in which the fourth respondent has been stated to be acquitted; as also the order of bail with respect to the latter case.
List on 04.10.2024, on which date, the fourth respondent and the alleged detenue shall remain present before this Court without fail.

2. Today, the Sri.P.M.Shameer - learned Government Pleader, affirmed that no Appeal has been filed against the judgment of the Court acquitting the 4 th respondent, but that proceedings for such has been initiated.
3. Obviously, as of now, there does not appear to be any further allegations against the 4th respondent.

2024:KER:73714 WP(Crl)1037/24 4. However, the petitioner and his wife, who were both personally present before this Court,
reiterated their extreme concern for their daughter, saying that she appears to be taking her decisions in an immature manner.
5. We certainly understand the angst of the parents, but we are also aware that the girl - alleged detenue, is over 18 years in age.
The law provides that she can take care of herself and we cannot impose any condition on her against her wishes.

In the afore circumstances, we close this Writ Petition without any further orders; however,
recording that the alleged detenue has informed us even today that she intends to continue with the 4th respondent.

Sd/-
DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN JUDGE Sd/-
